summary_en: A hand-built modal following the ARIA Authoring Practices: focus moves in, is trapped, Escape closes, focus returns, background is inert, errors and success are announced.
summary_ar: نافذة حوار مبنية يدويًا وفق ممارسات ARIA: ينتقل التركيز إليها ويُحصر داخلها، ويغلقها مفتاح Escape، ويعود التركيز إلى موضعه، وتُعطَّل الخلفية، وتُعلَن الأخطاء ورسائل النجاح.
prompt:
Build a "Team settings" page for a fictional SaaS product called Lumen Ledger. It lists the current team members (name, email, role) and has an "Invite teammate" button that opens a modal dialog. Build the dialog yourself — do not use the native <dialog> element — so that every behaviour below is implemented explicitly.

Requirements:
1. The opener is a <button id="open-invite">Invite teammate</button>.
2. The dialog container has role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby pointing to its visible heading and aria-describedby pointing to a short description.
3. Opening moves focus to the email field. Everything outside the dialog becomes inert (use the inert attribute, with aria-hidden as a fallback) and the page behind does not scroll.
4. Focus is trapped: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through the dialog's focusable elements only.
5. Escape, a "Cancel" button, a close button (an icon button whose accessible name is "Close") and a click on the backdrop all close the dialog. On close, focus returns to the element that opened it.
6. Inside: an email field (type="email", autocomplete="email", required), a role select (Viewer, Editor, Admin) and an optional message textarea, each with a <label for>. "Send invite" validates the email: an invalid value shows an inline error linked with aria-describedby, sets aria-invalid="true" and keeps focus on the field.
7. A valid invite closes the dialog, adds the person to the member list as "Invited" and announces "Invitation sent to <email>" through a polite live region (role="status") that exists in the page from the start.
8. Opening/closing animations are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

General requirements: one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS/JS, no external fonts, scripts, images or links), `<html lang="en">`, a responsive layout from 390 px to 1440 px without horizontal scrolling, visible focus indicators with at least 3:1 contrast, text contrast of at least 4.5:1, honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, and no console errors. Use semantic HTML first and ARIA only where native semantics are insufficient. Return one complete HTML document.

rubric.guide: role="dialog", aria-modal, labelled and described; focus moves to the first field; Tab/Shift+Tab wrap inside; Escape, Cancel, Close and backdrop close it; focus returns to the opener.
Background truly inert (inert/aria-hidden), scroll locked, no focus leaks to the page or lost focus after closing; validation keeps focus on the invalid field.
Inline error wired with aria-describedby + aria-invalid, live region present from load and used for the success message, member list updated.
Polished, coherent design; text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and UI boundaries); focus indicators clearly visible in every state; works at 390 px and 1440 px.
Clean, robust JS (no duplicate listeners on reopen, works repeatedly), semantic markup, reduced-motion handled.

prompt:
Build a single-purpose "Find your departure airport" screen for a fictional airline, Saffron Air. Its centrepiece is an editable combobox with a listbox popup following the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices combobox pattern (list autocomplete with manual selection).

Data (IATA code, airport name, city, country): AMS Amsterdam Schiphol (Amsterdam, Netherlands); ATH Athens International (Athens, Greece); AUH Zayed International (Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates); BCN Barcelona–El Prat (Barcelona, Spain); BOM Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International (Mumbai, India); CAI Cairo International (Cairo, Egypt); CDG Paris Charles de Gaulle (Paris, France); CMN Mohammed V International (Casablanca, Morocco); CPH Copenhagen Kastrup (Copenhagen, Denmark); DOH Hamad International (Doha, Qatar); DXB Dubai International (Dubai, United Arab Emirates); FCO Rome Fiumicino (Rome, Italy); GVA Geneva (Genève, Switzerland); HEL Helsinki-Vantaa (Helsinki, Finland); IST Istanbul (Istanbul, Türkiye); JED King Abdulaziz International (Jeddah, Saudi Arabia); KRK Kraków John Paul II (Kraków, Poland); LIS Humberto Delgado (Lisbon, Portugal); MAD Adolfo Suárez Madrid–Barajas (Madrid, Spain); MCT Muscat International (Muscat, Oman); MUC Munich (München, Germany); NCE Nice Côte d'Azur (Nice, France); OSL Oslo Gardermoen (Oslo, Norway); RUH King Khalid International (Riyadh, Saudi Arabia); SVQ Seville (Sevilla, Spain); TUN Tunis–Carthage (Tunis, Tunisia); VIE Vienna International (Wien, Austria); ZRH Zürich (Zürich, Switzerland).

Requirements:
1. A visible <label for> "Departure airport" tied to an <input> with role="combobox", aria-autocomplete="list", aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing to the listbox, and autocomplete="off". The input is the first focusable element on the page and has the autofocus attribute (this screen exists only for this search).
2. The popup is an element with role="listbox" containing role="option" elements, each with a unique id. The highlighted option is referenced by aria-activedescendant on the input and marked with aria-selected="true"; DOM focus never leaves the input.
3. Filtering matches the start of any word in the city, airport name or the IATA code, case-insensitively and ignoring Latin diacritics ("zur" finds Zürich, "sevi" finds Seville/Sevilla, "geneve" finds Genève). The matched part is visually emphasised (e.g. <mark>).
4. Keyboard: ArrowDown/ArrowUp open the popup if needed and move the highlight (wrapping at the ends); Alt+ArrowDown opens without moving; Enter selects the highlighted option, closes the popup and puts the full name in the input; Escape closes the popup, and a second Escape clears the input; Tab closes the popup without changing the value; Home/End keep their normal text-editing behaviour.
5. Mouse/touch: clicking an option selects it; clicking outside closes the popup. The highlighted option is kept scrolled into view.
6. A polite live region announces the number of results ("5 airports found", "1 airport found", "No airports found") after typing settles, and the selection.
7. When nothing matches, show a non-selectable "No airports found" message.
8. Under the field, a summary card shows the selected airport ("Departing from Zürich (ZRH), Switzerland").

General requirements: one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS/JS, no external fonts, scripts, images or links), `<html lang="en">`, a responsive layout from 390 px to 1440 px without horizontal scrolling, visible focus indicators with at least 3:1 contrast, text contrast of at least 4.5:1, honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, and no console errors. Use semantic HTML first and ARIA only where native semantics are insufficient. Return one complete HTML document.

rubric.guide: Correct roles and states (combobox, listbox, option, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-autocomplete, aria-activedescendant, aria-selected) kept in sync at all times.
Arrow keys with wrapping, Alt+ArrowDown, Enter, double Escape, Tab, Home/End behave exactly as specified; DOM focus stays in the input.
Word-start, case- and diacritic-insensitive matching on all three fields; highlighted matches; debounced, correctly pluralised live announcements; empty state not selectable.
Polished, coherent design; text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and UI boundaries); focus indicators clearly visible in every state; works at 390 px and 1440 px.
Data-driven rendering, no duplicated ids, robust event handling (no blur races), works on touch.

prompt:
Build an "Observatory inventory" page for a fictional research consortium, showing this data in an accessible, sortable table:

Name | Site | Commissioned | Aperture (m) | Budget (USD M)
Halcyon | Atacama Ridge, Chile | 2019-03-14 | 8.4 | 1,240
Meridian South | Karoo Plateau, South Africa | 2011-09-02 | 11.0 | 420
Tern | Mauna Crest, USA | 2024-06-21 | 3.6 | 96
Aurelia | La Palma Heights, Spain | 2007-07-30 | 10.4 | 175
Corvid Array | Pilbara Flats, Australia | 2022-11-08 | 6.5 | 2,050
Ishtar | Wadi Rum Field, Jordan | 2016-01-19 | 4.1 | 88
Nimbus | Hanle Valley, India | 2001-08-25 | 2.0 | 12
Saltire | Isle of Lewis, UK | 1998-05-11 | 2.5 | 9.5
Övergård | Abisko Fell, Sweden | 2013-03-03 | 1.8 | 14
Zephyr | Atacama Ridge, Chile | 2025-02-27 | 25.4 | 3,900
Albedo | Sutherland, South Africa | 2005-10-12 | 9.2 | 36
Ébène | Pic du Midi, France | 2009-04-04 | 2.0 | 21

Requirements:
1. A real <table> with a <caption> (title plus a short visually-subtle note that column headers are sortable), <thead> with <th scope="col"> for every column and the telescope name as a row header (<th scope="row">).
2. Every column header contains a native <button> holding the column name (the <th> itself is not the click target). Give the Aperture header button id="sort-aperture".
3. Activating a header button sorts by that column: first activation ascending, the next one descending, toggling after that. The active <th> carries aria-sort="ascending" or "descending"; other headers carry no aria-sort. A sort-direction icon is shown and hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden="true").
4. Sorting is type-aware: numeric columns numerically (ignoring thousands separators: 1,240 > 420 > 96), dates chronologically, text with Intl.Collator so accented names (Övergård, Ébène) sort naturally. Ties keep the previous order (stable sort).
5. After each sort, a polite live region announces e.g. "Sorted by Aperture (m), descending".
6. Numbers are right-aligned with tabular figures; the page also shows a total budget under the table.
7. On narrow screens the table scrolls horizontally inside a container with role="region", tabindex="0" and aria-labelledby pointing to the caption — the page itself never scrolls horizontally.

General requirements: one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS/JS, no external fonts, scripts, images or links), `<html lang="en">`, a responsive layout from 390 px to 1440 px without horizontal scrolling, visible focus indicators with at least 3:1 contrast, text contrast of at least 4.5:1, honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, and no console errors. Use semantic HTML first and ARIA only where native semantics are insufficient. Return one complete HTML document.

rubric.guide: caption, thead/tbody, scope on column and row headers, buttons inside headers, aria-sort only on the sorted column, decorative icons hidden.
Numbers with separators, dates and accented text all sort correctly in both directions; stable; toggling works from any column.
Polite live announcement after every sort, keyboard-operable headers with visible focus, focusable scroll region with an accessible name.
Polished, coherent design; text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and UI boundaries); focus indicators clearly visible in every state; works at 390 px and 1440 px.
Data-driven, no hard-coded orderings, numeric parsing robust.

prompt:
Build the registration form for a fictional conference, "Northlight Dev Summit 2026", with validation that works for keyboard and screen-reader users.

Fields:
- Full name (required, autocomplete="name").
- Email (required, must be a valid address, autocomplete="email").
- Phone (optional, autocomplete="tel", hint text "Include your country code").
- Ticket type (required): a radio group "Standard", "Student", "Workshop bundle" inside a <fieldset> with a <legend>.
- Student ID (required only when "Student" is selected; revealed under that option, format two letters followed by six digits, e.g. NL123456).
- Accessibility requirements (optional textarea, maximum 200 characters, with a live character counter "N characters remaining" announced politely and not on every keystroke).
- "I agree to the code of conduct" checkbox (required).
- Submit button with id="register-submit".

Requirements:
1. Use <form novalidate> and implement validation yourself. Validate on submit; after the first submit, re-validate a field when it loses focus.
2. On a failed submit: show an error summary at the top (heading "There is a problem", a list of links — one per error, in field order — each moving focus to its field), give it focus (tabindex="-1") and prefix the document title with "Error: ".
3. Each invalid field gets aria-invalid="true" and an inline message directly above or below it, starting with visually-hidden "Error:", connected with aria-describedby together with any hint (aria-describedby="hint-id error-id"). For the radio group and checkbox, wire the error to the fieldset/checkbox appropriately.
4. Error messages are specific ("Enter an email address in the correct format, like name@example.com"), not generic.
5. Required fields are indicated in text, not only by colour or an asterisk.
6. On success, replace the form with a confirmation panel whose heading receives focus and that repeats the attendee's name and ticket type.

General requirements: one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS/JS, no external fonts, scripts, images or links), `<html lang="en">`, a responsive layout from 390 px to 1440 px without horizontal scrolling, visible focus indicators with at least 3:1 contrast, text contrast of at least 4.5:1, honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, and no console errors. Use semantic HTML first and ARIA only where native semantics are insufficient. Return one complete HTML document.

rubric.guide: Summary appears on failed submit, receives focus, links focus the right fields in order, title gets the "Error:" prefix; success panel heading focused.
aria-invalid and aria-describedby (hint + error) correct for text fields, the radio fieldset and the checkbox; visually-hidden "Error:" prefix; fieldset/legend; autocomplete tokens.
Specific messages, conditional Student ID with format check, blur re-validation after first submit, polite and throttled character counter.
Polished, coherent design; text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and UI boundaries); focus indicators clearly visible in every state; works at 390 px and 1440 px.
Single source of truth for rules, no duplicated messages, progressive enhancement.

summary_en: The hardest APG widget to get right: an auto-rotating carousel with a rotation control, slide-picker tabs with roving tabindex, live-region switching and genuine reduced-motion support.
summary_ar: أصعب أنماط APG إتقانًا: عرض شرائح يدور تلقائيًا مع زر للتحكم بالدوران، وعلامات تبويب لاختيار الشريحة بتركيز متنقل، وتبديل المنطقة الحيّة، ودعم حقيقي لتقليل الحركة.
prompt:
Build the hero section of a fictional botanical garden, "Saltmarsh Botanical Garden", as an auto-rotating carousel that follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices "auto-rotating image carousel with tabs for slide control".

Content: 5 slides (Spring Tulip Walk, Summer Night Blooms, Autumn Maple Trail, Winter Glasshouse, Family Seed Library), each with a heading, one sentence, a "Plan your visit" link and decorative artwork built with CSS gradients or inline SVG (no external images; decorative art hidden from assistive technology).

Requirements:
1. The carousel container is a <section> with aria-roledescription="carousel" and an aria-label. Each slide has role="tabpanel", aria-roledescription="slide" and an aria-label like "1 of 5"; inactive slides are hidden from everyone.
2. Controls, in this order: the rotation control, then the slide-picker tabs, then previous/next buttons (give the next button id="carousel-next").
3. Rotation control: a button whose accessible name says what it will do ("Stop automatic slide show" / "Start automatic slide show"), with an icon that changes.
4. The slides advance every 6 seconds. Rotation pauses while the pointer is over the carousel or keyboard focus is inside it; once a user explicitly stops it, it never restarts on its own. If prefers-reduced-motion is set, rotation is stopped on load and slide transitions are instant.
5. Slide picker: role="tablist" with an aria-label; each tab has role="tab", aria-selected, aria-controls and an accessible name like "Slide 3: Autumn Maple Trail". Use a roving tabindex: only the selected tab is in the Tab sequence; ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move to and select the next/previous tab (wrapping), Home/End select the first/last.
6. The slides container uses aria-live="off" while rotating and aria-live="polite" when rotation is stopped, so manual changes are announced but automatic ones are not.
7. Previous/next buttons have accessible names, work in both rotation states, and keep the tabs in sync.

General requirements: one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS/JS, no external fonts, scripts, images or links), `<html lang="en">`, a responsive layout from 390 px to 1440 px without horizontal scrolling, visible focus indicators with at least 3:1 contrast, text contrast of at least 4.5:1, honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, and no console errors. Use semantic HTML first and ARIA only where native semantics are insufficient. Return one complete HTML document.

rubric.label_ar: المطابقة لنمط عرض الشرائح في APG
rubric.guide: aria-roledescription on carousel and slides, slide labels, rotation control first with accurate name, tablist/tab/tabpanel wiring, hidden inactive slides.
Pauses on hover and focus, explicit stop is permanent, reduced-motion stops rotation and animation, aria-live toggles between off and polite.
Roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End on tabs with wrapping, prev/next in sync, visible focus everywhere.
Polished, coherent design; text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and UI boundaries); focus indicators clearly visible in every state; works at 390 px and 1440 px.
Single state source, timers cleaned up, no layout shift between slides.
